title: Counting the Corneal Cells

patient.name: Mdm Tan Ah Lian
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for endothelial cell count — known Fuchs corneal dystrophy, scheduled for cataract surgery

history.hpc: Mdm Tan has Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (known for 5 years) and has now developed a visually significant cataract in the right eye. Before proceeding with cataract surgery, the doctor wants to know whether her corneal endothelial cell count is adequate to withstand the surgical trauma. She is referred for specular microscopy (endothelial cell count, ECC) of both eyes. She does not wear contact lenses. No previous eye surgery.
history.pmhx: Fuchs corneal dystrophy. Right eye cataract. Hypertension. No previous eye surgery.
history.social_hx: Retired. Lives with daughter. Does not drive.

va.right: 6/24 (LogMAR 0.6) — reduced by cataract and corneal oedema

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: corneal guttata (gold beaten appearance on retroillumination), early morning blurring reported by patient, nuclear cataract. Left eye: corneal guttata less dense, clear lens.
examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed — not the focus today

ecc_right.result: Severely reduced cell density. High risk for corneal decompensation post-operatively.

ecc_left.result: Moderately reduced. Lower than normal but may tolerate surgery better than right eye.

diagnosis: Endothelial cell count completed. Right eye: severely reduced (820 cells/mm2). Left eye: moderately reduced (1450 cells/mm2). Results to be reviewed by surgeon. Fuchs dystrophy patient — high risk for post-op corneal decompensation if cataract surgery proceeds on right eye without consideration for combined procedure (cataract + corneal transplant).

immediate: Confirm patient identity and both eyes to be examined
Explain the procedure: painless, uses a special camera to photograph the cells on the back of the cornea, about 5-10 minutes
Do not instil any drops before ECC unless ordered — topical anaesthetic may be required depending on machine
Set up specular microscopy machine and enter patient details
Position patient at chinrest with forehead on forehead rest
Align machine with central cornea, achieve focus, capture high-quality images
Ensure at least 100 cells are analysed in the sample for reliable count
Document cell density (cells/mm2), coefficient of variation, and hexagonality
Print report and hand to doctor
follow_up: Surgeon to review ECC results before planning cataract surgery
Surgeon may counsel patient regarding need for combined procedure or corneal transplant (DMEK/DSAEK)
Follow-up ECC in 6-12 months to monitor cell loss progression
patient_education: Explain what the test is looking for: counting the cells that keep her cornea clear
Tell patient the test is quick and does not involve drops or touching the eye (if non-contact method)
Explain that the results will help the doctor decide the safest plan for her eye surgery

key_points: Confirms patient identity and purpose of test (pre-op ECC for Fuchs dystrophy)
Asks if patient wears contact lenses (lenses can affect corneal thickness/ECC — remove before test)
Notes the clinical context: why ECC is needed (Fuchs + cataract surgery risk assessment)
Explains the procedure to the patient
Sets up specular microscope correctly and enters patient data
Achieves adequate focus and image quality on central cornea
Ensures sample size is adequate (minimum 100 cells for reliable density estimate)
Records all three key parameters: cell density (cells/mm2), coefficient of variation, hexagonality
Understands purpose: assessing corneal endothelial reserve before surgery
Recognises that low cell density (below ~1000 cells/mm2) carries higher surgical risk
Does not independently make clinical decisions — reports results to doctor
Identifies that Fuchs dystrophy means pre-existing cell dysfunction, increasing risk
Documents complete ECC report and prints/hands to doctor
Performs test on both eyes as ordered
Educates patient on what the test measures and why it matters for her surgery plan
Does not instil unauthorised drops before test
